result.summary: Full S1-S14 pass over REQ-023 (waitlist auto-promotion on a freed seat, T-24h halt), branch feature/WF02-REQ-023, commit f1dae51. Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md in full, then read domain/registration.ts, domain/event.ts, domain/user.ts, and handlers/withdraw.ts myself end to end -- not REVIEWER's summary -- and traced every call path by hand. Also re-ran npm run lint, npm run build, and npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism myself (see evidence.commands) -- all green, 211/211 tests. REVIEWER's flagged S10 question (does S10 actually name waitlist promotion as ignore-broadcast_opt_in-eligible) -- RESOLVED, no ambiguity. security-invariants.md S10's own text states verbatim: 'Transactional (admission result, WAITLIST PROMOTION, reminders, feedback request, event cancelled) is always sent, ignoring broadcast_opt_in.' This is not an inference from a broader category -- 'waitlist promotion' is named explicitly, word for word, as its own listed transactional item. No design correction or wording clarification is needed on this specific point; handlers/withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification correctly contains no broadcast_opt_in check anywhere in its path (confirmed by reading the full function, lines 178-219), matching S10's table by omission. However, re-deriving S10 in full (not just the flagged sub-question) surfaced a second clause in the SAME sentence that the design and implementation both missed: S10's very next sentence states 'blocked users are skipped in both cases' -- i.e. in BOTH the transactional and the marketing send path, unconditionally. Grepped the whole apps/bot codebase for the `blocked` column (users.blocked, schema.ts:80, a real, pre-existing, not-diff-introduced boolean) and for every call site: it is read/checked NOWHERE in this codebase today, including in this diff's new sendPromotionNotification / getUserForNotificationById. This diff is the FIRST code path in the entire bot that proactively addresses a Telegram chat_id belonging to someone other than the update's own ctx.from (REVIEWER's own report and the design's own §6.2 both flag this explicitly as a novel call-site shape) -- and it is exactly this kind of send that S10's blocked-skip clause exists to gate. getUserForNotificationById's SELECT (domain/user.ts:161-170) does not even project users.blocked, so sendPromotionNotification has no way to honor the rule even if it wanted to -- the data isn't fetched. Every prior 'transactional' message in this codebase (direct-admission confirmation, withdraw confirmation, etc.) is a ctx.reply() to the SAME chat that just messaged the bot, which is a fundamentally different risk shape (a blocked user cannot message the bot to trigger it in the first place) -- so this is not a pre-existing, structurally-unrelated gap; it is a gap this diff's own new send introduces into the one send shape where it actually matters (addressing an arbitrary chat_id the bot was not just spoken to by). Per core-directives 'in the diff is not the same as caused by the diff' -- but here the causal argument runs the other way too: this diff creates the first place S10's blocked clause could ever be violated, so it owns making that clause hold. This is a FAIL under S10: 'a broadcast segment that reaches an opted-out user because the segment query filtered on the wrong flag' (the file's own stated negative case) generalizes directly here -- the query filters on no flag for `blocked` at all, so a blocked user (someone who, per the column's evident purpose, should receive no further bot-initiated contact) would still be sent the promotion notification whenever they are the earliest-waiting waitlisted candidate. Everything else reviewed below is a genuine PASS; this is the sole blocking finding. S7 (capacity, atomic) -- PASS. Read promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible (registration.ts:361-446) line by line: `SELECT ... FROM events WHERE id = eventId FOR UPDATE` (lines 368-378) is the literal first statement, before any other read or write -- confirmed no prior line touches the DB. Confirmed this is the exact same lock discipline registerForEvent (REQ-020) already uses on the same table, so the two transactions serialize on the shared events row: whichever commits first releases the lock, the other's own admittedCount read (registration.ts:386-390) is then guaranteed fresh. Grepped the whole apps/bot/src tree for every UPDATE that sets admission to 'admitted': exactly two call sites exist -- registerForEvent's own write-outcome branch (registration.ts:203-224, gated by decideRegistrationOutcome) and promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible's step 5 (registration.ts:424-427). No third path, no bulk/admin/scheduled-job path exists anywhere that could promote a waitlisted row while bypassing this function's lock -- confirmed via a codebase-wide grep for `admission.*admitted` (see evidence.commands), and independently via `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/migrations apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` being empty (no new trigger/procedure could have been added either). Deadlock-order re-derived myself (not accepted from REVIEWER's report): withdrawRegistration's lock order is registrations(withdrawn row, line 508-518) -> events (via promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible, line 368) -> registrations(waitlist candidate, a distinct row, line 409-415); registerForEvent's order is events (line 123-135) -> its own caller's (event,user) row (written later, not locked earlier). The only resource contended by both is the single events row -- structurally cannot cycle. Ran registration.db.test.ts's own AC4 test myself: `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts -t 'AC4'` -> 20/20 iterations passed, admitted-row count never exceeded 1. S8 (audit, exactly one row) -- PASS. promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible contains exactly one writeAuditLog call (registration.ts:430-437), reached only after the decidePromotionEligibility 'ok:true' branch (line 402-404 returns early on every refusal reason -- event-not-eligible, halted-t24h, capacity-full -- with zero DB write and zero audit call before that point) AND after step 4's candidate SELECT finds a row (no-waitlist returns at line 418-420, also zero writes). Traced all four refusal paths by hand: none reaches line 424 (the UPDATE) or line 430 (the audit write). Re-ran the second-invocation-against-a-full-event scenario via reading §5's design argument against the actual code: a second call recomputes seatsLeft fresh (line 390) from the just-incremented admittedCount, refuses at decidePromotionEligibility row 3 (capacity-full) before step 4/5/6 -- zero new writes, confirmed by construction, not by trusting the design doc's prose. Authorization / cross-tenant leak of OTHER waitlisted people (new concern this task named) -- PASS. Read sendPromotionNotification (handlers/withdraw.ts:178-219) end to end: the composed message contains exactly catalog.promotion.admittedPrefix (static string), eventTitle (the promoted person's OWN event), dateTimeText (the same event's timing), the promoted person's OWN freshly-generated qrToken, and catalog.promotion.whatNext (static). No waitlist position, no count of other waitlisted people, no other user's id/name/tgId ever enters this function's scope -- getUserForNotificationById is called once, for the promoted person's own userId only (line 185), and getEventIdForRegistration/getEventByIdWithChapterTimezone read only event-level fields (title/dates), never registrations rows. Confirmed candidateRows (registration.ts:409-416, the SELECT that finds the promotion target) is never passed anywhere near the notification composition beyond the single promoted candidate.id/userId already returned in PromotionOutcome -- the other two (or more) waitlisted rows in AC1's 3-person scenario are never read by step 4's own LIMIT 1 query in the first place, let alone surfaced to anyone. T-24h halt as an adversarial-timing-proof guarantee -- PASS. isAutoPromotionHalted (event.ts:744-746) takes both startsAt and evaluationTime as explicit parameters and reads neither from the wall clock -- confirmed by reading the full function body (one arithmetic subtraction and comparison, no `new Date()`, no SQL now()). decidePromotionEligibility (registration.ts:330-344) calls it with the SAME evaluationTime it itself received as a parameter -- no second, independent clock read exists between the halt check and any other step. Traced the full chain: handlers/withdraw.ts:130 reads `new Date()` exactly once, threads it as `at` into withdrawRegistration, which threads it unchanged as `evaluationTime` into promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible (registration.ts:364), which threads it unchanged into decidePromotionEligibility (line 400) and into the audit write's `at` (line 436). There is no window between 'read starts_at' (event.ts:372, part of the same FOR UPDATE row read at step 1) and 'evaluate the halt' where a second, later clock read could disagree with the first -- both startsAt and evaluationTime are fixed, in-memory values by the time decidePromotionEligibility runs; no adversary-controlled input (registrationId, callback timing, retry) can change which evaluationTime value reaches the halt check, since it is derived once, server-side, before the transaction begins. Boundary convention (<=24h halted, >24h eligible) matches AC1 (48h, not halted) and AC2 (12h, halted) exactly as designed and tested. S1 -- N/A, reason: no new personal data is stored or consent-checked; the promoted row's qr_token is regenerated (not newly collected) and admission is the only column written. S2 -- PASS -- no role/organizer/EventStaff dimension is touched; promotion is system-initiated (actorUserId: null, the existing precedent) against a row selected purely by waitlist order, not by any caller-suppliable id. S3 -- PASS -- see the cross-tenant-leak analysis above; only the promoted person's own data is ever read or sent. S4 -- PASS -- the promoted row's qr_token is generated via the SAME generateQrToken() CSPRNG call (32 bytes/256 bits, randomBytes) reused verbatim from REQ-020, never derived from the user id or any predictable input; the promoted row's OLD (none -- waitlisted rows never had a token) value is irrelevant, a fresh token is always minted at promotion time (registration.ts:423). S5/S6 -- N/A, check-in code (checkin.ts) is untouched by this diff (confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts apps/bot/src/domain/checkin.ts` -> empty). S7 -- PASS (see above). S8 -- PASS (see above). S9 -- PASS by construction, not merely asserted -- idempotency here is DB-state-derived (the row's own admission transition), not an in-memory set that a restart would clear: once step 5 commits, the row's admission is 'admitted' and step 4's WHERE admission='waitlisted' filter can never re-select it, on any process restart, retry, or duplicate job run, because there is no in-memory-only marker anywhere in this mechanism. The one gap the design itself names (§5's closing paragraph) -- a crash between commit and the Telegram send actually completing, which is an at-least-once-delivery gap, not an idempotency-of-STATE gap -- is correctly out of scope for REQ-023 and explicitly deferred to REQ-025's future outbox ledger; not a defect of this diff. S10 -- FAIL (see above) -- the promotion notification does not check users.blocked before sending, and getUserForNotificationById does not even select that column, so the invariant's 'blocked users are skipped in both cases' clause cannot currently hold for this send. The broadcast_opt_in half of S10 (REVIEWER's flagged question) is correctly satisfied. S11 -- PASS -- grepped the diff's changed files for console/log calls: zero matches. The audit payload for registration.promote contains only `{ eventId }` (registration.ts:435), no phone/email/name/tgId. The promotion notification itself is a Telegram message TO the data subject about their own registration, not a log -- not an S11 concern. S12 -- N/A, no export code touched. S13 (migration sign-off, named duty) -- N/A, no migration in this diff. Confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat` (no apps/bot/drizzle/*.sql file) and independently via a glob for apps/bot/src/db/migrations/**/*.sql -- no results, matching the design's own explicit 'no schema change' claim, re-verified against the current schema.ts rather than trusted from the design doc. S14 -- N/A, no publication/speaker code touched. Commands run myself, real output: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing, unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (Next.js build + apps/bot tsc). `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, full suite) -> 17 files / 211 tests passed, 0 failed. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts` -> 50/50 passed, confirming REQ-022+REQ-023's own DB-backed suites (including the 20-iteration AC4 concurrency test) pass against a live Postgres, not skipped (dbAvailable path taken, no `t.skip()` triggered). Verdict: FAIL on S10. Route back to BACKEND-DEV: add a `blocked: users.blocked` projection to getUserForNotificationById (domain/user.ts) and a guard in sendPromotionNotification (handlers/withdraw.ts) that skips the send (same silent-skip shape already used for the null-tgId guard) when the promoted person's row has `blocked === true`. This is a implementation-level fix, not a design-level one -- REQ-023.md's design should also be updated (a MINOR note, not blocking re-design) to state the blocked-skip explicitly in §6.2 alongside the broadcast_opt_in-ignore rule, so a future notification send in this codebase does not repeat the same omission.

commands: git diff master...HEAD --stat -> 15 files changed, matches the design's own file list + handoff/design bookkeeping
git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/migrations apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts -> empty, confirms no schema change
grep -rn "admission.*admitted" apps/bot/src -> exactly two SET-clause writers of admission='admitted' (registerForEvent, promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible), no third/bulk/admin path
grep -rn blocked apps/bot/src -> zero call sites anywhere in the codebase read/check users.blocked; only schema.ts declares the column
npm run lint (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web warnings
npm run build (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces clean
npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root) -> 17 files / 211 passed, 0 failed

invariant_results.S1: N/A -- no new personal data stored or consent-checked
invariant_results.S2: PASS -- no role/organizer/EventStaff dimension; promotion targets a row selected only by waitlist order, actorUserId: null (system-initiated, existing precedent)
invariant_results.S3: PASS -- promotion notification carries only the promoted person's own event/qrToken data; other waitlisted people's rows are never read or surfaced
invariant_results.S4: PASS -- fresh generateQrToken() CSPRNG call at promotion time, same 256-bit randomBytes mechanism as REQ-020, never derived from predictable input
invariant_results.S7: PASS -- events-row FOR UPDATE is the first operation in promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible, serializing against registerForEvent's identical lock; exactly two admission='admitted' writers exist codebase-wide, both gated by this discipline; deadlock order re-derived safe
invariant_results.S8: PASS -- exactly one writeAuditLog call, reached only on the sole write-worthy branch, same transaction as the UPDATE; every refusal path (event-not-eligible/halted-t24h/capacity-full/no-waitlist) returns before any write
invariant_results.S9: PASS -- idempotency is DB-state-derived (the row's own one-way admission transition), not an in-memory marker a restart would clear; the one named at-least-once-delivery gap (post-commit send failure) is correctly deferred to REQ-025, not a defect here
invariant_results.S10: FAIL -- broadcast_opt_in half correctly ignored per S10's explicit naming of 'waitlist promotion' as transactional (resolves REVIEWER's flagged question with no ambiguity); BUT the 'blocked users are skipped in both cases' clause in the same S10 sentence is not implemented -- getUserForNotificationById does not select users.blocked, and sendPromotionNotification sends unconditionally regardless of it. This diff is the first code path in the codebase that proactively addresses a chat_id other than the current ctx.from's own, making it the first place this clause could ever be violated.
invariant_results.S11: PASS -- zero log/console calls in the diff; audit payload contains only eventId
invariant_results.S13: N/A -- no migration in this diff, confirmed via diff stat and migrations glob

evidence.s10_flagged_question_resolution: security-invariants.md S10 names 'waitlist promotion' verbatim, as its own listed item, inside the parenthetical of transactional categories that ignore broadcast_opt_in -- not an inference from a broader category, an explicit, unambiguous match. No design correction or wording clarification needed on the broadcast_opt_in half. The blocking finding is a DIFFERENT clause in the same S10 paragraph (the blocked-skip requirement), which REVIEWER's flagged question did not ask about but which this SECURITY-REVIEWER pass is required to check independently per the 'run every applicable item' mandate.
evidence.cross_leak_check: sendPromotionNotification's composed message contains only the promoted person's own eventTitle/dateTimeText/qrToken plus static catalog strings; no other waitlisted person's id, name, or position ever enters scope. Confirmed by reading handlers/withdraw.ts:178-219 and registration.ts's candidate-selection query (only the single LIMIT-1 row's id/userId are returned in PromotionOutcome).

issues.title: Waitlist-promotion notification does not skip blocked users (S10)
issues.description: security-invariants.md S10 requires 'blocked users are skipped in both cases' (transactional AND marketing sends). handlers/withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification (the new post-commit send introduced by REQ-023) sends unconditionally once a promotion occurs, with no check of users.blocked. domain/user.ts's getUserForNotificationById does not even project the blocked column, so the send path has no way to honor this rule as currently written. This is the first code path in apps/bot that proactively messages a chat_id other than the current update's own ctx.from, so it is also the first place in the codebase capable of violating this clause. Fix: add `blocked: users.blocked` to getUserForNotificationById's projection, and skip the send in sendPromotionNotification when the promoted person's row has blocked === true (same silent-skip shape as the existing null-tgId guard). REQ-023.md's design (§6.2) should also gain an explicit line stating the blocked-skip requirement, matching how it already states the broadcast_opt_in-ignore rule, so this is not silently re-omitted by a future notification send.

result.next_action: Route back to BACKEND-DEV to add the users.blocked skip to the promotion notification path (S10), then re-run Step 2b/2c before TEST-DESIGNER.
